title: Feature-Guided SAE Steering for Refusal-Rate Control using Contrasting Prompts

analysis.Inference & Systems (S): The paper implements feature-guided steering during inference to control refusal rates, involving systems-level interventions such as modulating feature strengths without speculative decoding or quantization.
analysis.Alignment, Safety & Governance (A): Central to the paper, focusing on refusal-rate control for unsafe prompts while complying with safe ones, directly addressing safety alignment through SAE steering without refusal training or watermarking.
analysis.Data & Inputs (I): The paper uses contrasting prompts from the AI-Generated Prompts Dataset (teknium/OpenHermes-2p5-Mistral-7B) and Air Bench eu-dataset for feature selection, indicating data-driven inputs for safety alignment.
analysis.Optimization & Training Recipe (R): No evidence of optimization or training recipes discussed; the method is applied post-training without mentions of optimizers, schedulers, or parallelization strategies.
analysis.Architecture & Modeling (M): The method employs Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) for interpretable feature extraction from LLMs, specifically applied to Llama-3 8B, focusing on model internal representations without altering the base architecture.
analysis.Evaluation & Benchmarks (E): Evaluation conducted on Llama-3 8B, reporting 18.9% safety improvement and 11.1% utility increase, implying use of benchmarks to measure safety-utility tradeoffs, though specific suites are not detailed.
analysis.Objectives & Learning Signals (O): Not directly addressed; the steering approach does not introduce new training objectives or learning signals but leverages existing features for inference-time control without weight adjustments.

analysis.Robustness & Safety (R): Evaluates stability across random seeds and fairness across products, and notes the avoidance of excessive price volatility, indicating attention to robustness against variability and safety in pricing decisions.
analysis.Collective Evaluation (E): Assesses collective metrics such as profit, stability, and fairness across products, reflecting social welfare, resource efficiency, and emergent behavior in the multi-product portfolio.
analysis.Team Formation & Role Specialization (S): Not addressed; the paper treats product agents homogeneously without role assignment, dynamic coalition formation, or specialization, focusing instead on coordinated pricing decisions.
analysis.Learning Dynamics (L): Uses multi-agent reinforcement learning (MAPPO) with self-play and adaptation to shifting demand, evaluated for training efficiency and stability across random seeds, demonstrating equilibrium learning in a non-stationary environment.
analysis.Mechanism & Incentive Design (M): Not addressed; the approach focuses on learning pricing policies directly rather than designing mechanisms to elicit truthful signals or efficient outcomes under strategic behavior.
analysis.Interaction Protocols (P): The paper employs graph-attention mechanisms in MAPPO to enable learned communication and coordination among product agents, facilitating information sharing over the product graph without explicit negotiation protocols.

analysis.Objectives & Learning Signals (O): The paper formulates medical error handling as three subtasks (detection, localization, correction) serving as learning signals, and uses targeted LoRA fine-tuning to improve error correction performance with specific objectives.

title: Leveraging Hierarchical Image-Text Misalignment for Universal Fake Image Detection

analysis.Alignment, Safety & Governance (A): Addresses fake image detection to prevent malicious use, implying safety applications, but no explicit alignment, red-teaming, or governance techniques are discussed.
analysis.Data & Inputs (I): Utilizes image-text pairs from datasets, leveraging pre-trained CLIP's joint visual-language space. Inputs include whole images and semantic objects from captions for hierarchical misalignment analysis.
analysis.Optimization & Training Recipe (R): Mentions tuning an MLP head for detection, but no specific optimizers, schedulers, or training recipes are detailed in the abstract.
analysis.Architecture & Modeling (M): Employs pre-trained CLIP as the backbone for multimodal alignment, with an added MLP head tuned for detection. The hierarchical scheme models global and local semantic misalignment without architectural modifications to CLIP.
analysis.Evaluation & Benchmarks (E): Conducts extensive experiments demonstrating generalization and robustness across various generative models, indicating use of benchmarks for evaluation against state-of-the-art methods.
analysis.Objectives & Learning Signals (O): Primary objective is binary classification for fake image detection. Learning signal is derived from image-text misalignment in CLIP space, used to train the MLP head without explicit pretraining losses.

title: Region-Aware Reconstruction Strategy for Pre-training fMRI Foundation Model

analysis.Inference & Systems (S): Inference and systems aspects such as serving stacks, batching, quantization, or distillation are not discussed in the abstract. The evaluation focuses on classification tasks without deployment considerations.
analysis.Alignment, Safety & Governance (A): Alignment, safety, and governance considerations are not addressed in the abstract. The study is methodological and does not mention red-teaming, safety tuning, or ethical constraints.
analysis.Data & Inputs (I): Uses resting-state fMRI scans from the ADHD-200 dataset (973 subjects) with full 4D volumes. Implements ROI-guided masking strategy based on the Automated Anatomical Labelling Atlas (AAL3) for selective masking of semantically coherent brain regions during pre-training.
analysis.Optimization & Training Recipe (R): No details on optimizers, schedulers, parallelism, or training strategies are mentioned in the abstract. The paper centers on the masking approach without specifying optimization techniques.
analysis.Architecture & Modeling (M): The abstract does not specify the model architecture; it focuses on the masking strategy rather than backbone design or attention variants. Reconstruction-based pre-training is used, but no details on transformer or other architectures are provided.
analysis.Evaluation & Benchmarks (E): Evaluates on the ADHD-200 dataset for classification accuracy (4.23% improvement in distinguishing healthy controls from ADHD) and conducts region-level attribution analysis to identify contributions from limbic region and cerebellum. Uses reconstruction fidelity as a metric for representation quality.
analysis.Objectives & Learning Signals (O): Employs self-supervised reconstruction objectives with region-aware masking. The loss involves reconstructing masked anatomical regions to improve representation learning, as indicated by reconstruction fidelity metrics and the focus on semantically coherent regions.

title: ToxicTextCLIP: Text-Based Poisoning and Backdoor Attacks on CLIP Pre-training

analysis.Inference & Systems (S): Not a focus; evaluation involves inference tasks, but the paper does not explore serving stacks, batching, or inference optimizations.
analysis.Alignment, Safety & Governance (A): The paper investigates poisoning and backdoor attacks on CLIP, testing and bypassing safety defenses like RoCLIP, CleanCLIP, and SafeCLIP, highlighting vulnerabilities in alignment and governance.
analysis.Data & Inputs (I): The paper focuses on generating adversarial texts to poison CLIP pre-training data, using a background-aware selector and augmenter to ensure semantic coherence and evade detection, addressing data quality and filtering challenges.
analysis.Optimization & Training Recipe (R): Not covered; no details on optimizers, schedulers, or training recipes are provided.
analysis.Architecture & Modeling (M): Not addressed; the paper assumes CLIP's standard architecture without modifications or novel modeling contributions.
analysis.Evaluation & Benchmarks (E): Extensive experiments on classification and retrieval tasks measure poisoning success (up to 95.83%) and backdoor Hit@1 (98.68%), benchmarking against defenses and evaluating adversarial risks.
analysis.Objectives & Learning Signals (O): Not discussed; the attack exploits CLIP's contrastive learning objective but does not alter it or introduce new learning signals.

title: DRIP: Defending Prompt Injection via De-instruction Training and Residual Fusion Model Architecture

analysis.Inference & Systems (S): No discussion of inference systems, serving stacks, batching, quantization, or related optimizations in the abstract.
analysis.Alignment, Safety & Governance (A): Focuses on defending against prompt injection attacks through training-time safety tuning, reducing attack success rates, and enhancing model security against adaptive threats.
analysis.Data & Inputs (I): No explicit discussion of raw data corpora, tokenization, or data preprocessing methods in the abstract. The 'token-wise de-instruction shift' is part of the training objective rather than data input handling.
analysis.Optimization & Training Recipe (R): Mentions a training-time defense but provides no details on optimizers, schedulers, parallelism, or other training recipe components in the abstract.
analysis.Architecture & Modeling (M): Proposes a residual fusion pathway as an architectural modification to provide a persistent semantic anchor, reinforcing the true top-level instruction during generation and enabling robust separation between instruction and data semantics.
analysis.Evaluation & Benchmarks (E): Evaluates performance on prompt injection benchmarks (SEP, AlpacaFarm, InjecAgent) and utility benchmarks (AlpacaEval, IFEval, MT-Bench), demonstrating improved role separation and attack resistance while maintaining utility.
analysis.Objectives & Learning Signals (O): Introduces de-instruction training for semantic disentanglement, weakening directive semantics in data tokens while preserving content meaning, and employs role-aware supervision to enforce separation between instruction and data semantics.

title: Friend or Foe: How LLMs' Safety Mind Gets Fooled by Intent Shift Attack

analysis.Data & Inputs (I): The paper generates attack prompts by transforming harmful intents into benign-seeming requests using minimal edits, creating natural, human-readable inputs and datasets for experiments, which relates to data augmentation and quality.
analysis.Optimization & Training Recipe (R): Minimally covered; fine-tuning models on ISA templates is mentioned, but no specific optimizers, schedulers, or training strategies are detailed in the abstract.
analysis.Architecture & Modeling (M): Not covered; the paper focuses on attacking pre-existing LLM architectures rather than proposing or modifying model designs, with no mention of architectural changes.
analysis.Evaluation & Benchmarks (E): Extensively covered; the paper conducts experiments on open-source and commercial LLMs, measures attack success rates, evaluates defenses, and uses benchmarks to assess safety vulnerabilities and efficacy.
analysis.Objectives & Learning Signals (O): The attack exploits weaknesses in how models learn to recognize harmful intent, and fine-tuning on ISA-reformulated data involves adjusting learning signals for safety, relating to objective design and preference learning.

title: EraseFlow: Learning Concept Erasure Policies via GFlowNet-Driven Alignment

analysis.Data & Inputs (I): Not explicitly detailed in abstract, but implied use of diffusion models for text-to-image generation, with concepts erasure applied to existing model priors.
analysis.Optimization & Training Recipe (R): Optimization specifics not detailed, but involves training GFlowNets with trajectory balance to learn erasure policies without prohibitive retraining.
analysis.Architecture & Modeling (M): Uses GFlowNets to model denoising trajectories in diffusion-based generation, casting concept erasure as exploration in the space of denoising paths.
analysis.Evaluation & Benchmarks (E): Extensive empirical evaluation demonstrates outperformance over baselines and optimal trade-off between erasure performance and prior preservation.
analysis.Objectives & Learning Signals (O): Employs trajectory balance objective from GFlowNets to learn stochastic policies for concept erasure, eliminating need for reward models and adversarial losses.

analysis.Robustness & Safety (R): Robustness is implied through multiple trajectory generation and self-correction in the Generation Agent, but no explicit measures for adversarial agents, collusion, or sybil attacks are mentioned.

analysis.Team Formation & Role Specialization (S): Roles are explicitly specialized: Grounding Agent for schema linking, Generation Agent for query generation via RL, and Validation Agent for final selection based on generation probability, forming a fixed team structure without dynamic coalition formation.
analysis.Learning Dynamics (L): The Generation Agent uses a multi-turn RL policy with a ReAct-style Think-Act-Observe loop, enabling iterative self-correction based on execution feedback from a live database, handling non-stationarity through stateful reasoning and exploration of diverse trajectories.
analysis.Mechanism & Incentive Design (M): Not addressed; no mechanisms for eliciting truthful signals or managing strategic behavior are described. The Validation Agent's selection based on generation probability lacks incentive alignment features like VCG mechanisms.
analysis.Interaction Protocols (P): The framework employs a pipelined workflow where agents sequentially interact: Grounding Agent processes schema linking, then Generation Agent generates queries, and Validation Agent selects the final output. There are no explicit inter-agent communication protocols; coordination is structured through this sequential pipeline.

title: Align to Misalign: Automatic LLM Jailbreak with Meta-Optimized LLM Judges

analysis.Architecture & Modeling (M): No specific model architecture is introduced; the framework employs a bi-level meta-optimization structure for joint evolution of prompts and templates, but relies on pre-existing LLMs like Claude.

analysis.Objectives & Learning Signals (O): Objectives include maximizing attack success rate (ASR) and aligning scoring templates using ASR alignment scores, with fine-grained feedback serving as dense learning signals in the inner loop.
